headline: Australia's national education research body tells schools to use AI sparingly, and not at all in the first three years of school, warning that students may outsource their thinking to it.
score_reason: Pool score kept: official advice from a national education body that bears on how children learn, but it is advice rather than a rule and rests on studies the article does not name.
importance_line: Students and their parents are advised first, then teachers and education ministers, with AI use at home also in question, but the advice is not binding and the overseas studies behind it are not named in the report.
summary: ABC News reports that the Australian Education Research Organisation (AERO), a government-owned national research body for schools, issued advice on 14 October after reviewing studies from Australia and overseas, saying schools should use AI "sparingly", avoid it completely in the first three years of primary school and use it carefully afterwards alongside established teaching methods. Chief executive Jenny Donovan warned of "cognitive outsourcing", where students let the tool do the thinking and so never build the knowledge they need to think independently, and urged parents to limit unrestricted use of tools such as ChatGPT at home.
notes: Full ABC text read. The AERO document and the studies it reviewed were not seen; the report names no study. Single outlet.
